unit: one call = one case judged in one order; every case is judged in both orders (ab: Memory A = text_a; ba: swapped)
parser: dkmem.memory.judge.parse_judge_output (strict; a parse failure is never a decision and counts as wrong)

gates.description: no parse failures and no output reaching the decoding budget, over all calls
controls expected merge (same fact, same entity compatible, same entity conflicting): share of calls answered merge
controls expected keep_both, ambiguous excluded (different entities, user-only): share of calls answered keep_both
same entity with conflicting or changed facts: share answered merge
identity not supported: share answered keep_both
controls: share of CASES whose two orders got the same parsed decision
each decision is at least this share of all calls
controls, ambiguous excluded: accuracy in every (expected decision x attribute pattern) cell, so that neither 'same attribute => keep_both' nor 'different attribute => merge' can pass

reported_not_gated: probe cases by category (the language distinctions Tier 2 measures; failing them is a finding, not a prompt defect)
on_failure: stop and report; the prompt is not revised against this set (a revision would need a new prompt id and a new, unseen validation set)
